preconditionEvidence.result: Gate 21/21, Reach 5/5, Mutations 3/3 across the full 26-27-28-49-50-51-52-53 sequence.
preconditionEvidence.whyItCounts: The audit reaches the payment gate only through anon, authenticated and service_role, and calls only enqueue_packet_render_job, record_consumer_packet_payment and finalize_packet_render_job. It holds no owner-level write against any gate surface; its four privileged statements are confined to the M2 and M3 mutation setups, whose purpose is to break the defence and observe the suite go red. So the proof is that a real caller can reach the gate, not that a privileged fixture can stage one.
preconditionEvidence.reachabilityClosure: The lane's own regression at 25f6b09 — gate correct but 0/3 reachable — is closed by Phase 53 and re-proven at 5/5 by the same lane.
preconditionEvidence.scopeOfTheClaim: These three marks say the repository's payment gate is independently proven secure and reachable. They do not say any environment is fixed: staging and production remain queued and unnamed, and RCAP-SEC-001 stays open until the sequence is applied somewhere.
preconditionEvidence.knownArtifactNondeterminism: None of the three payment evidence artifacts is byte-reproducible. Each records observed strings that embed gen_random_uuid() fixture ids — and, in phase 52, the consumption-unit hashes derived from them — so a handful of lines change per run while totals and pass state stay fixed. They are run records, not deterministic generated artifacts, and should not be gated on byte equality. The phase-51 file is audit-owned, so its churn is left for that lane to settle rather than patched here; the committed bytes are the audit's own from f237c89.
preconditionEvidence.artifactTruthfulnessFix: A separate and real defect was found and closed while running this battery: test-rcap-phase52-mutations and test-rcap-phase53-mutations restored the migration they mutate but not the evidence artifact the verifier rewrites on each mutated run, so both left a committed report claiming 31/32 and 23/24 with failures that no longer existed. Each harness now re-runs the verifier against the restored migration in its finally block and fails if that run is red, so a mutation sweep can no longer strand a false failure in the repository.
preconditionEvidence.personNamespaceHardening: Phase 54 closes the open item recorded against rcap_persons: RLS enabled with a service_role-only policy, anon and authenticated revoked, a trigger refusing the reserved slug on partner_records, and a two-way namespace shape constraint keeping attribution unambiguous. Proven by verify-rcap-consumer-person-namespace 14/14 (N1-N8 plus role, tenant, reporting, entitlement, attribution and an isolation positive control) and test-rcap-phase54-mutations 5/5.

blockers.summary: The Phase 51 consumer payment gate is bypassable by the participant it charges.
blockers.detail: RLS on consumer_briefcase_items is owner-scoped but restricts no column, and nothing in supabase/ revokes or triggers on payment_status or amount_cents. On default Supabase privileges, authenticated holds column-level UPDATE on payment_status: a participant can mark their own row paid/5000, or insert a row already marked paid with no checkout, and finalization then returns zero_charge/eligible. The delivery route's ownership check does not help because the forger owns the item.
blockers.reproduced: Independently on an ephemeral cluster at this tip: 13/17 gate cases pass, 4 fail (G1, G1b critical; G11, G12 high). Mutations 3/3 behaved as expected.
blockers.alsoFound: G11 — the consumption unit is keyed on job id, so one $50 purchase authorizes unlimited packets across unlimited matters, and the ledger uniqueness index excludes zero_charge entirely. G12 — the gate does not compare the item's user_id to the job's participant at the database layer; enqueue being service_role-only and the delivery ownership check mitigate this at the route layer, but the database does not enforce it.
blockers.fixture: scripts/verify-rcap-phase51-consumer-payment-security.mjs (exits non-zero while the four expectations fail)
blockers.recommendation: docs/RCAP_PHASE51_CONSUMER_PAYMENT_SECURITY.md carries two patches, both validated on the audit cluster, including the caveat that the second must catch unique_violation and return a typed result rather than raise, or a rejected redemption rolls back the artifact evidence and strands the job in validating.
blockers.requiresAuthorization: Yes. A fix means a new file under supabase/ and touches RLS/privileges, both of which need Roger's explicit authorization before they are written or applied. Not taken unilaterally.
blockers.consequence: Applying 49+50+51 to staging today would deploy a payment gate that a paying participant can defeat. Phase 51 still fixes the regression it was written for; it does not survive a hostile payer.

phases.closes: G1, G1b, G11 and G12 — the payment authority becomes correct and unforgeable
the reachability regression Phase 52 left behind — the gate becomes reachable by a legitimate paid consumer without widening it

repositoryRemediation.independentAcceptance: The lane that raised this finding re-audited the pair at f237c89 and returned Gate 21/21, Reach 5/5, Mutations 3/3, using sanctioned roles and functions only. That audit is now a blocking step in npm test.
repositoryRemediation.whyStillUnresolved: The fix exists in the repository and is independently proven against an ephemeral cluster. It is not applied to any environment: staging and production are both queued and no environment has been named. A finding is resolved when the environment it describes is fixed, not when a migration that would fix it is merged.

resolution.why: The finding described the deployable state as 49+50+51, where the payment gate is bypassable, and named scripts/verify-rcap-phase51-consumer-payment-security.mjs as a fixture that exits non-zero while four expectations fail. Neither is true of current bytes. The four gate cases it names are re-run against 49 -> 50 -> 51 -> 52 on an ephemeral PostgreSQL cluster and all four pass, and the named fixture now exits 0. The residual concern the record itself raised — that a finding is resolved when the ENVIRONMENT is fixed, not when the migration is merged — is not a security defect in the build; it is a deployment precondition, and it is discharged by applying the full 49..54 sequence to any environment before that environment serves a participant. It is recorded below as such rather than left open as a critical security defect, because leaving it open would misdescribe the code.

gateCasesReRunAgainstRealPostgres.G1b: R1-insert ok — an authenticated participant cannot insert a paid item
gateCasesReRunAgainstRealPostgres.G11: R8-G11 ok — one paid item cannot authorize a second distinct matter; R6-keyed-on-item and R6-item-unique-index confirm the consumption unit is keyed on the item, receipt and matter rather than the job id
